newsitem.title: USA: Operation Rescue founder runs for Congress.
newsitem.headline: Operation Rescue founder runs for Congress.

text.p: Randall Terry, founder of the anti-abortion group Operation Rescue, announced Monday he would run for Congress next year.
In his announcement speech, Terry said he would run in the Republican primary in the hope of challenging Democratic Representative Maurice Hinchey.

Using the slogan "You pay for it," Terry attacked the welfare system, "homosexual propaganda in government schools" and unwed mothers. He said he wanted the federal income tax abolished and the Social Security system made voluntary.
Terry promised to fight for "legal protection for preborn babies" and fight against "militant homosexuals who are trying to destroy the institution of marriage and seduce our sons and daughters."
Terry and Operation Rescue became known in the 1980s for staging protests at abortion clinics across the country.

"Although I do not know him and have not had the opportunity to meet him, he does have the reputation for intemperate behaviour and the statements he made today confirm that reputation," Hinchey said.
